title: Lamna Healthcare Company
sections: Lamna Healthcare Company operates a network of 2,400 outpatient clinics in nine European countries. The headquarters is in Stockholm, and the IT department has 140 employees. Lamna plans to replace its call-center scheduling process with a multi-agent assistant that patients and clinic staff use through the Lamna patient portal and Microsoft Teams.

**Identity and collaboration**

Lamna uses Microsoft Entra ID for all employees. Clinic staff use Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 Apps. Management reports are built in Power BI.

**Azure environment**

- A Microsoft Foundry account named Foundry1 in Sweden Central uses the Standard setup with bring-your-own resources: an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL account, an Azure AI Search service, and an Azure Storage account. All three resources are owned by Lamna.
- Foundry1 has a provisioned throughput deployment named PTU1 and a Standard deployment named Standard1 of the same model and version.
- A second Foundry account named Foundry2 in West Europe has a provisioned throughput deployment named PTU2 that the disaster recovery team uses for quarterly failover tests.
- The network uses a hub-and-spoke topology. The hub virtual network contains Azure Firewall, which inspects all outbound internet traffic from the spokes.

**Agents in development**

- A scheduling agent books, moves, and cancels appointments for patients.
- An intake agent reads referral letters that external clinics and partner hospitals upload as PDF files, and drafts referral summaries for clinic staff. The intake agent has read-only access to the referral store.
- A summarization model drafts the referral summaries. The model will be fine-tuned on de-identified referral summaries.

- The network team plans to add a private endpoint to Foundry1 and to disable public network access.
- The data team plans to store the conversation turns of the scheduling agent in a new container in the existing Cosmos DB account.
- The AI team plans to run a supervised fine-tuning job for the summarization model once per month, after clinical reviewers approve a new batch of examples.
- Lamna plans to replace the legacy appointment reminder service with SMS messages that are sent by a separate team next year.

- Patients must be able to book appointments at any time. On Monday mornings between 07:00 and 09:00, traffic is three times the weekly average and exceeds the capacity of PTU1. Requests during these peaks must not fail.
- The scheduling agent is latency-sensitive, and its normal traffic is predictable.
- Clinic staff must be able to review the referral summaries in Teams.
- Lamna wants to minimize the cost of the solution where this does not conflict with other requirements.

**Network**

- Agent traffic to Cosmos DB, Azure AI Search, and Storage must stay on the private network to prevent lateral movement and data exfiltration.
- Outbound internet traffic from the agents must be inspected by the hub Azure Firewall.

**Conversation data**

- Each clinic is a tenant. Each clinic runs many concurrent conversation threads, and the largest clinics already store more than 20 GB of conversation data.
- Queries for one clinic must not scan the partitions of other clinics.
- Conversation turns must be deleted automatically 30 days after their last update.

**Security**

- A red team test showed that a referral letter that contains hidden white text can make the intake agent reveal its instructions. This risk must be reduced by using defense in depth.

**Fine-tuning**

- Training data for the summarization model must stay in the region of Foundry1 during training.
- Queue time for the monthly training job is less important than compliance.

- Lamna must not move patient data to resources that it does not own.
- The operations team does not want to manage Kubernetes clusters.
- Changes to Foundry2 require approval from the disaster recovery team.
